results.draft_locus: From Place to Seller ¶1
results.finding: 'The five answers in Ingrid's table failed for one reason' sums up the chapter from its opening complaint (conclusion_summary).

results.draft_locus: whole chapter
results.finding: Both readers describe the declared prerequisite order (problem, vocabulary, licence constraint, architecture, query semantics, cases, then judgements); neither marks any section's position unclear. Both noted the Agence Rhône Habitat detail in the hand-off as minor and not confusing, so it is not recorded as a lost-thread point.

results.draft_locus: Concepts ¶1
results.quote: These four kinds are not the three representations named in the callouts: a kind says what is located, a representation says how precisely one location is stored and shown.
results.finding: The meta-clarification sends the reader back to the callouts for a term (representations) the body defines only in the Architecture section; both readers stopped and re-read here. The spec's order is fine; the sentence anticipates a concept the reader does not yet hold.
results.corroborated_by: flowB item B2 (same sentence, meta-aside sends reader back to the key points)

results.draft_locus: Architecture ¶3 (after Architecture ¶2)
results.quote: Back to the table's order: each part can be recomputed from the parts above it: the public point from the precise point and the policy, the place references from the public or precise point and the gazetteer.
results.finding: The GDPR and Productscape paragraph (p22) interrupts the value-object table and the recomputation point that depends on it; the signpost admits the detour and the double colon makes readers reread. Both readers propose moving p22 after p21 or out of the subsection. The spec prescribes the order p20, p22, p21 and the Productscape evidence in place (decision log: both orders tried), so the difficulty comes from the spec's order and content.
results.corroborated_by: flowB item B5 (GDPR/Productscape paragraph breaks the flow; 'Back to the table's order' read twice)

results.draft_locus: Architecture, Figure 2 caption (before Architecture ¶4)
results.quote: Everything to the right of the precision policy engine (component 5 below) sees only what the policy allows, while duplicate detection and fraud models read the restricted store (component 6) through an audited path.
results.finding: The figure and its caption refer to numbered components before the list that numbers them; both readers had to look ahead. Placing the figure after the list (or not numbering in the caption) fixes it without touching the spec.
results.corroborated_by: flowB item B4 (Figure 2 caption cites components 5 and 6 before the list)

results.draft_locus: In Practice at Veldmark ¶1
results.quote: Her listing went live on the old model, a few weeks before the complaint. The six steps below are a replay: they show how the same listing is processed under the precision policy Veldmark adopted later in 2027.
results.finding: Both readers had to reconcile three dates (7 March, the late-March complaint, the policy 'later in 2027') and work out whether Femke was the scene's complainant (she listed a bike; the complainant a sofa). The spec's case order is fine; the prose does not state plainly that Femke is a different seller from the complainant and which model each step shows.
results.corroborated_by: flowB item B7 (three dates to reconcile; reread to see Femke is not the complainant)

results.draft_locus: In Practice at Veldmark ¶2
results.quote: Not every risk Femke met that evening was a location one: at 20:11 a "buyer" sent her a fake payment link, a messaging and fraud problem covered in [[messaging-and-leads]].
results.finding: Both readers read the fake-payment-link aside as leaving the topic and breaking the case's conclusion. The aside is prescribed by p44's evidence item and kept by the decision log, so the difficulty comes from the spec's content.
results.corroborated_by: flowB item B8 (aside that leaves the topic)

results.draft_locus: From Place to Seller ¶1
results.quote: The Lyon page that left out Villeurbanne had a different cause, no place references to choose between, and the same model's third representation fixes it.
results.finding: After 'The five answers in Ingrid's table failed for one reason', the synthesis turns to a second cause for an example that was not in Ingrid's table (it came from the introduction and the query section); one reader stopped at the shift from 'one reason' to 'a different cause', the other mistook the Lyon page for the Lyon apartment case. The spec's synthesis prescribes this two-cause structure tied to the five answers.
results.corroborated_by: flowB item B9 (Villeurbanne not in Ingrid's table; 'one reason' gives way to a second cause)

results.draft_locus: Trade-offs ¶1
results.quote: Veldmark's cases rest on three choices: where to store location (three representations suit multi-country groups), which geo index fits which job (engine-native types for queries, H3 for aggregation), and how to derive the public point (each method trades privacy against map quality; a snapped or seeded point, coarsened in sparse areas, balances the two).
results.finding: Flow reader A could not parse three verdicts packed into parentheses in one pass. Reported by one reader only.

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶2
results.quote: Part II models the listing as a small aggregate that references governed subdomains by ID ([[listing-aggregate]]).
results.finding: Flow reader B found the opening sentence dense with jargon and cross-links, burying the claim 'Location is not an attribute but a small subsystem'. Reported by one reader only.

results.draft_locus: Concepts ¶9
results.quote: The place levels, from country down to street, also name levels of detail.
results.finding: Flow reader B noted that the gazetteer paragraphs listed places down to neighbourhoods, never streets, so the bridge claims a level that was not introduced. Reported by one reader only.

results.draft_locus: Architecture ¶12
results.quote: The one exception is real estate: there the search document may also hold a precise `geo_point` that is never returned in responses but is used for polygon queries when the agency has chosen exact display.
results.finding: Flow reader B re-read: if the agency chose exact display, why is the public point not already precise? The prose does not say. Reported by one reader only.

results.draft_locus: Architecture ¶2
results.quote: The real-estate Productscape domain model, used in this book's research, classifies its geo reference data as internal and non-personal, but the listing that carries a private owner's location as "possible-personal".
results.finding: Productscape is named as evidence without saying what it is (whose model, published or not); the reader cannot weigh the evidence. Flow reader A reported it as an unexplained term.
results.corroborated_by: flowA item A2 ('The real-estate Productscape domain model, used in this book's research' unexplained term in an aside)
